claims.text: The Sealed Secrets controller holds a key pair; kubeseal encrypts a Secret's values with the public half (a certificate), and only the controller's private half decrypts them.
claims.source_hint: Sealed Secrets README: Overview, How it works; docs/developer/crypto.md

claims.text: kubeseal --cert <file> seals using the certificate from a file, with no connection to the cluster; --format yaml prints the SealedSecret as YAML.
claims.source_hint: Sealed Secrets README: Usage / Public key / Certificate (offline sealing with --cert); kubeseal --help

claims.text: seal-secrets.sh pipes kubectl create secret generic ... --dry-run=client -o yaml into kubeseal --cert secrets/sealing.crt --format yaml, writing envs/staging/sealed-<name>.yaml in the config repo clone; line 29 seals db, later lines api, keycloak and the other services.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/seal-secrets.sh:14-42

claims.text: seal-secrets.sh commits the sealed files and pushes them to the Git server, then waits for Argo CD to sync; its output lists each Secret in donhang with owner kind SealedSecret.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/seal-secrets.sh:63-70; outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/seal-secrets.txt

claims.text: A SealedSecret keeps its metadata name and namespace readable and holds the values as ciphertext under spec.encryptedData; spec.template.metadata gives the name and namespace of the Secret to create (apiVersion bitnami.com/v1alpha1).
claims.source_hint: Sealed Secrets README: SealedSecrets as templates for secrets; outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/seal-secrets.txt

claims.text: Argo CD applies a SealedSecret to the API server unchanged, like any manifest, and needs no decryption key; the controller creates the Secret.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Operator Manual > Secret Management (destination-cluster secret management, Bitnami Sealed Secrets)

claims.text: The controller watches SealedSecrets, decrypts each and creates a Secret of the same name in the same namespace; it records the SealedSecret as the Secret's owner in its metadata (ownerReferences).
claims.source_hint: Sealed Secrets README: Overview, SealedSecrets as templates for secrets; outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/seal-secrets.txt (OWNER SealedSecret)

claims.text: Pods read the controller-made Secret as any Secret; the database Pod's manifest still names db and reads POSTGRES_PASSWORD (secretKeyRef).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 deploy/gitops/config-repo/envs/staging/db.yaml:34-38 (secretKeyRef db/POSTGRES_PASSWORD)

claims.text: By default (strict scope) the SealedSecret's name and namespace are part of what is encrypted, so a copy with another namespace or name cannot be decrypted and no Secret is created.
claims.source_hint: Sealed Secrets README: Scopes (strict is the default)

claims.text: sealed-secrets-install.sh line 34 changes only the namespace with sed; the API server accepts both; line 38 lists Secrets named scope-demo in all namespaces (only donhang); line 40 prints the copy's status message 'no key could decrypt secret (word)'.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/sealed-secrets-install.sh:23-40; outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/sealed-secrets-install.txt

claims.text: kube-system is the namespace Kubernetes keeps for its own system components. The script's kubectl adds --context kind-donhang-staging (line 7, outside the excerpt); kube-system holds one Secret with the sealing-key label: sealing-key, state active.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Namespaces (initial namespaces, kube-system); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/sealed-secrets-install.sh:7, 18-20; outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/sealed-secrets-install.txt

claims.text: dev-secrets.sh creates the sealing key pair secrets/sealing.key and secrets/sealing.crt (openssl req -x509, RSA 4096) once per learner; secrets/ is gitignored.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/dev-secrets.sh (lesson: devops.l3.sealed-secrets block); STAGE.md 'Nothing under secrets/ ... is committed'

claims.text: The donhang-platform module installs both halves as Secret sealing-key in kube-system, type kubernetes.io/tls, label sealedsecrets.bitnami.com/sealed-secrets-key=active, which tells the controller to use it; the platform layer's (encrypted) OpenTofu state therefore holds a copy.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 deploy/tofu/modules/donhang-platform/main.tf (sealing_key); Sealed Secrets README: Bring your own certificates; OpenTofu docs: State

claims.text: By default the controller periodically generates a new sealing key; --key-renew-period=0 disables renewal. Đơn Hàng's controller manifest passes --key-renew-period=0, so the pre-installed key stays the only one.
claims.source_hint: Sealed Secrets README: Secret Rotation / Sealing key renewal; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 deploy/sealed-secrets/controller.yaml:45

claims.text: The private key decrypts every SealedSecret sealed with its certificate, so whoever holds secrets/sealing.key can open every SealedSecret in the config repository.
claims.source_hint: Sealed Secrets README: Overview; Bring your own certificates

claims.text: Holding the certificate allows sealing but gives no way to decrypt; the certificate is meant to be shared.
claims.source_hint: Sealed Secrets README: Public key / Certificate ('the certificate (public key portion) ... can be safely shared')

claims.text: kubectl create secret generic ... --dry-run=client -o yaml only prints the object; nothing is sent to the API server.
claims.source_hint: kubectl reference: kubectl create secret generic (--dry-run=client)

claims.text: Sealing is randomized (a fresh session key per seal), so sealing the same value with the same certificate twice gives different ciphertext; sealed guesses therefore cannot be compared with the file in Git.
claims.source_hint: Sealed Secrets docs/developer/crypto.md (random session key, RSA-OAEP + AES-GCM)

claims.text: Inside the cluster only the controller uses the private half, read from the Secret sealing-key in kube-system; Argo CD never gets it. Outside the cluster the same key also sits in secrets/sealing.key and the platform state (claims 12, 13).
claims.source_hint: Sealed Secrets docs: Bring your own certificates (label sealedsecrets.bitnami.com/sealed-secrets-key=active); Argo CD Operator Manual: Secret Management; deploy/tofu/modules/donhang-platform/main.tf

claims.text: For sealing, seal-secrets.sh reads .env and, of the key pair, only secrets/sealing.crt; it also reads secrets/donhang-tls.crt/.key when platform/edge exists (lines 49-54, not about the sealing key).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/seal-secrets.sh

claims.text: The host scripts that seal (seal-secrets.sh, sealed-secrets-install.sh) need kubeseal 0.40 installed on the host, as STAGE.md lists.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 STAGE.md (host tools list); content/versions.yaml sealed_secrets.kubeseal
